name: Shi Nengkeng
current_role: Reported founder and (as of 2015) chairman of Fujian Xunxing Group / Fujian SBS Zipper Science & Technology (SZSE: 002098), Jinjiang, Fujian; current role unverified
profile: Shi Nengkeng (施能坑) is reported as the founder of the Shi family's Xunxing Group in Jinjiang, Fujian, whose SBS brand grew from the Jinjiang Hualian Zipper Factory (1984) into one of China's largest zipper makers, listed in Shenzhen as 002098. Xunxing Group was the listed company's controlling shareholder. Little English-language information on him is available.
interesting_fact: The company's 'SBS' brand is said to stand for the brothers and sisters of the founding family. Xunxing also sponsors Jinjiang's CBA basketball club, the Fujian SBS Xunxing Sturgeons.
notes: Very low-profile private Chinese entrepreneur with almost no English coverage. Unofficial wiki mirrors name 'Nengkeng Shi' as founder/chairman, but I could not verify his current role from an official source (Baidu Baike was blocked). The SBS 'brothers and sisters' explanation comes from a search summary. The best route is likely via the listed company's investor relations (SZSE 002098).

name: Raghuram Shetty
current_role: Managing Director and co-promoter, Heranba Industries Ltd (NSE: HERANBA), Vapi, Gujarat
profile: Raghuram K. Shetty co-founded Heranba Industries in 1992 with his brother Sadashiv K. Shetty, who is chairman. Based in Vapi, Gujarat, Heranba grew into one of India's larger makers of crop-protection chemicals (synthetic pyrethroids, intermediates and formulations) and listed on the NSE/BSE in 2021. He remains MD, and the next generation now sits on the board.
interesting_fact: Heranba now has plants at Vapi and Sarigam and a greenfield site coming up at Saykha, Gujarat. In January 2026 it announced plans for a UAE subsidiary to make and trade crop-protection and nutrition chemicals.
notes: His profile is low-key and I found no personal social media or interviews. corporate@heranba.com is a company address, not a personal one. MarketScreener says he studied at the University of Mysore. That is unverified, so I left it out of the facts.

name: AVS Raju
current_role: Deceased (13 Oct 2026). He was Founder and Chairman Emeritus of NCC Limited (formerly Nagarjuna Construction Company), Hyderabad.
profile: Dr Alluri Venkata Satyanarayana Raju, founder of NCC Limited and a Padma Shri awardee, died in Hyderabad on 13 October 2026, aged 89.
notes: Died 13 Oct 2026 (Construction World, 14 Oct 2026). NCC also disclosed to the exchanges that he ceased to be a promoter. Per the instructions, I skipped the rest of his profile.

name: Gong Xiaodong
profile: Listed as the source of wealth for Yaobo Industry (China). I found no English or Chinese web sources linking a Gong Xiaodong to a company called Yaobo, so I could not confirm his identity or role.
notes: I could not identify him. I searched in English and under the likely Chinese spellings (宫晓东/龚晓东 + 耀博) and got nothing relevant. This probably needs the Chinese characters from the original list, or a Chinese company-registry lookup (Qichacha/Tianyancha), which was out of scope.

name: Hu Bo
profile: Listed as the source of wealth for Zhaojia Group (China). Hu Bo (胡波) is a very common name, and I found no sources tying a Hu Bo to a Zhaojia Group, so I could not establish who this is.
notes: I could not identify him: the name is too common and the company name is unmatched. I tried English and Chinese searches (胡波 + 兆嘉集团). This needs the original Chinese characters, or the company's city and industry.

name: Yamunadutt Amilal Agrawal
current_role: Founder and Chairman (non-executive), Jindal Worldwide Ltd (NSE: JINDWORLD), Ahmedabad
profile: Dr Yamunadutt Agrawal founded Jindal Worldwide, an Ahmedabad textile group that calls itself one of India's largest denim makers. It also makes bottom-weight, shirting and yarn-dyed fabrics and home textiles, and exports to the Americas, Europe, Africa and the Middle East. He has been non-executive chairman since 2011, and his son Amit Agrawal runs the company as vice chairman and MD.
interesting_fact: The company says its denim business made it India's largest denim manufacturer. It produces 400-500 fabric designs a month in a vertically integrated operation with about 3,000 staff.
deep_cut_fact: He trained as a medical doctor (MD in medicine) before spending 40 years in textiles. He sits on the advisory board of Gujarat's Textile Committee, is vice chairman of the Agrasen Foundation and Maharaja Agrasen Vidhyalaya, and has represented the Gujarat government at summits in the UK, China, Italy, Hong Kong and Singapore.
notes: Not to be confused with the steel and power Jindal family (JSW/Jindal Steel); this is a separate Ahmedabad textile company. Day-to-day leadership sits with his son Amit Agrawal (MD). Only the generic company email is published.

name: Peter Juhas
current_role: Chief Financial Officer, AerCap Holdings N.V. (NYSE: AER), Dublin
profile: Peter Juhas has been CFO of AerCap, the world's largest aircraft lessor, since April 2017, after joining as deputy CFO in 2015. Before that he was AIG's Global Head of Strategic Planning, where he worked on the 2014 sale of ILFC to AerCap. Earlier he spent 11 years as a Morgan Stanley investment banker and was an M&A lawyer at Sullivan & Cromwell. His wealth comes from executive pay and AerCap equity.
interesting_fact: At Morgan Stanley he was lead advisor to the Federal Reserve Bank and U.S. Treasury on the 2008 AIG restructuring, and on placing Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac into conservatorship.
deep_cut_fact: Long before becoming its CFO, he led AerCap's own 2006 IPO as a Morgan Stanley banker. He then helped sell AIG's ILFC to AerCap in 2014, the deal that made AerCap the industry giant.
notes: Corporate executive (not a founder). He has a Harvard A.B. in economics and a Harvard J.D. Media enquiries go through AerCap corporate communications (Dublin). The best route is probably IR, since he is the CFO.

name: Eric H. L. So
current_role: Co-founder and Director, Helus Pharma Inc. (formerly Cybin Inc.; Nasdaq/Cboe CA: HELP). In Oct 2026 he moved from executive chair/interim CEO to a board-only seat.
profile: Eric So co-founded Cybin in 2019 with Paul Glavine. Cybin develops psychedelic-derived serotonin-pathway drugs for depression and anxiety and rebranded as Helus Pharma in 2026. He was executive chairman and president, and returned as interim CEO in April 2026. In October 2026 he stepped back to the board as Mark Lawson became independent chair, ahead of Phase 3 data for HLP003.
interesting_fact: Helus's lead program, HLP003, holds FDA Breakthrough Therapy Designation, and pivotal Phase 3 data is expected in Q4 2026.
deep_cut_fact: He trained as a lawyer (LLB), not a scientist. Before Cybin he was VP Strategy and General Counsel at Synergex Corp (2006-2010), and he co-founded the boutique merchant bank Trinity Venture Partners.
notes: Cybin's legal name became Helus Pharma Inc. on 1 Oct 2026. His step-back to the board comes from a secondary news site (Panabee, 27 Oct 2026); confirm on ir.helus.com, which blocked automated fetch. The deep-cut career details come from MarketScreener, an aggregator. Some company bios called him a chemist, which conflicts with his LLB.

name: Hu Xiangen
profile: Listed as the source of wealth for Cixing Group (China). I found no sources linking a Hu Xiangen to a Cixing Group. The best-known 'Cixing' is Ningbo Cixing Co. (300307.SZ), a knitting-machine maker founded by Sun Pingfan, so this is probably a different company or a romanization mismatch.
notes: I could not identify him from English or Chinese (胡祥根 + 慈星) searches. Don't assume he is linked to Ningbo Cixing (300307), whose founder is a different person. This needs the original Chinese characters or a registry lookup.

name: Adam J Katz
current_role: Co-Founder and CIO, Irenic Capital Management LP (activist hedge fund, New York); CEO and director, Irenic Acquisition Corp. (SPAC)
profile: Adam Katz spent 2013-2021 at Elliott Management, then co-founded the activist fund Irenic Capital in 2021 (about $2.5bn AUM as of March 2026). Irenic's campaign at Barnes Group put him on its board in 2024, before Apollo bought Barnes for $3.6bn (closed Jan 2025). In 2026 he launched an aerospace and defense-focused SPAC and pushed for changes at Snap and Big Yellow.
interesting_fact: Institutional Investor named him one of its ten 'Hedge Fund Rising Stars' in 2023. He holds an HBS MBA (Baker Scholar) and a Harvard JD.
deep_cut_fact: After graduating from Harvard in 2007 he co-launched the women's e-commerce company FabFitFun, later backed by Kleiner Perkins, NEA and Upfront Ventures. He kept running it through 2011 while earning his MBA and JD.
notes: His Barnes Group directorship ended when Apollo acquired the company in Jan 2025; he is also on the boards of Arconic (since 2023) and KX Topco. Irenic's website has no published contact. The best route is likely the Irenic SPAC's SEC filings, or press contacts named in Irenic campaign releases.

name: Benjamin Wood
current_role: Chief Operating Officer, Cardinal Infrastructure Group Inc. (Nasdaq: CDNL)
profile: Benjamin 'Benji' Wood was vice president of A.L. Grading Contractors (ALGC), a Sugar Hill, Georgia site-work contractor with 300+ staff. Cardinal Infrastructure Group bought ALGC for $245.5M in February 2026 to enter Georgia and South Carolina, and Wood became Cardinal's COO. Cardinal is a fast-growing Southeast civil and site-development contractor, a segment tied to the data-center and industrial build-out.
interesting_fact: ALGC, which he helped run, won site work on a Walmart sorting facility after joining Cardinal. Cardinal's 2025 revenue was expected at about $452-460M, roughly 45% growth on 2024.
notes: Lee Wood Jr. (ALGC president) joined Cardinal's board. A conference recap reportedly calls them brothers, but I could not confirm that from a primary source. I found no published IR or press email in the pages I checked. The IR site (investors.cardinalinfrastructuregroup.com) is the best route. Site development is a good angle for the data-center podcast.

name: Anders Gustafsson
current_role: Chair of the Board, Zebra Technologies (ZBRA); director of NetApp (NTAP) and International Paper (IP), where he chairs the audit committee
profile: Swedish-born executive Anders Gustafsson was CEO of Zebra Technologies from 2007 to March 2023, turning the barcode-printer maker into an enterprise mobile-computing and data-capture company. He is now Zebra's chair. Before Zebra he was CEO of Spirent Communications (2004-07) and held executive roles at Tellabs and Motorola. He also sits on the NetApp and International Paper boards.
interesting_fact: Under his leadership, Zebra bought Motorola Solutions' Enterprise division (including Symbol Technologies and Psion) for $3.45 billion in 2014. The deal turned Zebra into a major player in rugged mobile computers.
deep_cut_fact: He is an engineer by training, with an MSc in electrical engineering from Chalmers University of Technology in Gothenburg, Sweden, plus a Harvard MBA. He is also a trustee of Chicago's Shedd Aquarium and on the Commercial Club of Chicago's Civic Committee.
notes: Chicago-based. His NetApp board seat ties in with the data-center and storage theme. The Zebra press contact (Therese Van Ryne, Sr Director External Communications) and IR email appear in the 2026 press releases; I saw them via search snippets, not a direct page fetch.

name: Michael W Koehnen
current_role: Vice Chairman and Corporate Secretary, TriCo Bancshares / Tri Counties Bank (Chico, CA); Owner and President, C.F. Koehnen & Sons (Ord Bend, CA)
profile: Michael Koehnen is a Northern California agribusiness owner. He runs C.F. Koehnen & Sons, a fourth-generation farming and beekeeping company, and the almond processor Riverwest Processing, along with related export companies in Glenn County. He has been a TriCo Bancshares director since 2002, vice chairman since 2010 and corporate secretary since 2021, and is a long-time significant shareholder.
interesting_fact: The Koehnen family has kept bees since 1907 and is one of the world's largest producers of honey bees and queen bees. Its colonies are around Glenn County in the Northern Sacramento Valley.
deep_cut_fact: Koehnen's Italian queens are all light-coloured 'Cordovan' bees, from a breeding project begun around 1975. The family has produced Italian queens since the 1930s, and they make up about two-thirds of its queen production.
notes: Private, rural agribusiness owner with no personal media presence. The Koehnen bee-business contact form is a commercial channel, so use it sparingly. TriCo's corporate secretary office is the formal route. He is not an energy or data-center figure; his wealth is agriculture plus TriCo stock.

name: Eric Venker
current_role: Chief Executive Officer, Immunovant (IMVT), since April 2025; President, Roivant Sciences (ROIV)
profile: Eric Venker, MD, PharmD, is a physician-turned-biotech operator. He joined Vivek Ramaswamy's Roivant in 2014 and rose through chief medical officer, chief of staff and COO to president. In 2025 he also became CEO of Immunovant, Roivant's majority-owned FcRn-antibody company developing batoclimab and IMVT-1402 for autoimmune diseases.
interesting_fact: He trained in internal medicine at NewYork-Presbyterian/Columbia. There he led operational-efficiency initiatives across a hospital system with $5 billion in annual revenue, before moving into biotech.
deep_cut_fact: Before medical school he was a clinical pharmacist at Yale-New Haven Hospital. He holds a Pharm.D. from the St. Louis College of Pharmacy as well as an M.D. from Yale School of Medicine.
notes: Roivant handles Immunovant's IR and media, so the listed contacts are Roivant staff. Sources differ on when he became Roivant president (2018 per Immunovant, 2021 per aggregators).

name: Jason T Liberty
current_role: Chairman and Chief Executive Officer, Royal Caribbean Group (NYSE: RCL)
profile: Jason Liberty became Royal Caribbean Group's CEO in January 2022, after nine years as CFO, and later also became chairman. He led the company out of the pandemic shutdown and into record results. Its brands are Royal Caribbean, Celebrity and Silversea, plus a 50% stake in TUI Cruises, with a fleet of 71 ships and nearly 100,000 employees. He also sits on the Southwest Airlines board.
interesting_fact: Under him, the group has expanded beyond ships into exclusive private destinations and a new river-cruise line, Celebrity River Cruises. The company also highlights 'energy innovation' as a strategic priority, which fits the podcast's energy angle.
deep_cut_fact: He began his career at KPMG and holds three degrees: a BBA in accounting from the University of Miami, a master's in finance from Indiana University and an MBA from UNC Kenan-Flagler. He now serves on the University of Miami Board of Trustees and Kenan-Flagler's Board of Advisors.
notes: High-profile, media-friendly CEO based in Miami. Corporate Communications is the right route. The energy and decarbonisation angle (LNG ships, new fuels) is a natural hook for the podcast.
